claims.claim: Mastercard's durable structural role is an interoperability, trust and routing layer connecting consumers, issuers, merchants and digital partners; current wallet and agentic-commerce launches extend that coordination layer rather than proving a new standalone profit pool.

The causal chain is human need for trusted low-friction exchange -> merchant/issuer interoperability and fraud controls -> Mastercard network/tokenization/data infrastructure -> acceptance and partner network effects; substitutes can weaken individual rails, but broad endpoint and partner connectivity makes replacement more likely to be gradual than binary.

Scenario robustness is strongest where commerce remains fragmented across institutions, currencies, wallets and channels; it weakens if account-to-account, closed-loop, stablecoin or sovereign rails achieve comparable acceptance, dispute, identity and fraud tooling without Mastercard intermediation.

factors.name: bottleneck control
factors.basis: Mastercard coordinates acceptance, routing, tokenization/security and partner connectivity across a large multi-sided payments ecosystem.

factors.name: scenario robustness
factors.basis: Digital-payment fragmentation preserves demand for interoperable trust/routing layers across cards, wallets and emerging agentic interfaces.

factors.name: substitution resilience
factors.basis: Network effects and security tooling raise switching friction, while account-to-account, closed-loop, stablecoin and sovereign rails remain credible substitute paths.

causalEdges.mechanism: buyers and sellers require common trust, identity, settlement and dispute primitives
issuers, merchants and digital partners use shared network and security capabilities to transact across fragmented endpoints
broader connectivity increases usefulness to each side of the network

causalEdges.from: substitute rails with equivalent trust and acceptance
causalEdges.mechanism: equivalent lower-cost routing/security can reduce dependence on incumbent card-network economics

risks.risk: Substitute rails could commoditize portions of routing economics if they match acceptance, security, identity and dispute capabilities.
New wallet and agentic connectivity can strengthen network relevance without producing proportionate incremental economics.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental transaction volume, pricing and margin attributable to Wallet Pay and Agent Connect remain undisclosed.
Long-run share of commerce that bypasses card-network intermediation through alternative rails is uncertain.

claims.claim: The strongest present challenge is not that Mastercard lacks execution, but that product-launch breadth can be mistaken for proven incremental economics; current evidence establishes connectivity and distribution intent, not transaction ramp or margin contribution.

Regulatory and competitive pressure are persistent structural risks because Mastercard sits in a high-value intermediary layer; however, the evidence reviewed does not establish a present contradiction severe enough to block Beta closure.

A valid falsifier for the resilience thesis would be sustained migration toward substitute rails that deliver comparable acceptance, security and dispute handling while materially reducing Mastercard's transaction relevance or pricing power.

factors.name: confidence inflation risk
factors.basis: Named partners and launches are evidence of availability/distribution, not proof of scaled economics.

factors.name: regulatory exposure
factors.basis: Payment-network economics remain exposed to antitrust, interchange and settlement pressure.

factors.name: competitive substitution
factors.basis: Alternative rails can bypass portions of the network, while Mastercard continues extending connectivity into wallets and newer commerce interfaces.

risks.risk: Launch/partner counts may overstate commercial traction before volume and economics are disclosed.
Regulatory remedies can compress network economics or constrain commercial practices.
Cyber/fraud failures would attack the trust primitive on which network utility depends.
Alternative payment rails can reduce card-network relevance in specific corridors or use cases.

unknowns.unknown: Current incremental revenue and margin from Wallet Pay and Agent Connect are not source-addressed in the reviewed evidence.
No reviewed evidence quantifies current share loss to substitute rails by corridor/use case.
